rv.q: The scene in which these two misfits meet is breathtaking—awkward and funny, scary and sad, electric and erotic—and Desmond and White imbue their characters with a discomfort so realistic that watching them feels almost voyeuristic.

What follows is a delirious, unpredictable theatrical experience, which begins as anthropology and then unveils itself as something more provocative: an exploration of the possibilities and limits of human intimacy.
Degenerates is a brave, ambitious, sad and sexy beast of a play, imperfect in the way of something gnarly and long-wrestled-with, nevertheless gripping as a piece of performance.
Else Went has a sure touch for dialogue and event, particularly across extremely long scenes; she has a precise ear for the sadness under the bluster.
Degenerates is an early contender for this season’s best.
Daring to go deep into psychosexual discomfort, the Wents' play illuminates the annihilative consequences of loneliness and self-loathing in a corrosive subculture.
Degenerates is fascinating, at times startlingly suspenseful.
Else Went’s Degenerates is a difficult play for many reasons and not an easy play to like.
Degenerates gives us a glimpse under their hood, but doesn’t answer the questions it raises.
Despite their frequently nasty talk – the playwright churns up some surprisingly funny invective – the characters are not degenerates so much as pathetic in their self-loathing loneliness.
Like those award-winning plays, there is much that is well-observed in “Degenerates,” and some moments that are bracingly theatrical.
No actor, however, could make the ridiculous transition that Went’s play requires of Desmond.
This is engrossing, essential theater that should not be missed.
It is an impressive, multi-layered piece of writing and an absolute must-see.
Ultimately, the play delivers a beautiful lesson about loneliness, the human need for connection, and the courage it takes to embrace love—a lesson worth learning.
Else has written a play with no easy answers.
The show’s biggest achievement is that it lets us relate to characters we entered the theater believing were depraved.
Degenerates is a marvelously unpredictable, moving, and surprising story that gives voice to those in need even as they reject, or are rejected by, so-called societal norms.
Degenerates is a significant work not meant for the faint of heart.

cn.t: Critics praise Went's intense, daring deep-dive into incel culture as brilliant and electrifying, though some find it overwhelming or overly sympathetic. Strong performances and extensive research earn acclaim despite concerns about length and density.

vr.q: I truly think Degenerates is one of my favorite plays of the year.
Degenerates is definitely going to be a Broadway Ben must see.
Go check out Degenerates at Playwrights if you want to be challenged by some really thought-provoking, edgy theater
This methodically slow and sizzling piece drops you into an existence with these characters that's so insular, it almost feels like a simulation.
